---
title: "Data generation for logistic regression model under controlled conditions"
---

# Overview

This simulation compares three bisection algorithms for selecting coefficients
in a logistic model:

| Algorithm | Quantity adjusted | Quantity held fixed | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Intercept | Slope multiplier = 1 | Prevalence |
| 2 | Slope multiplier | Intercept = 0 | C-statistic (AUC) |
| 3 | Intercept and slope multiplier | Relative slope sizes | Both targets |

The model is

$$
p_i = \operatorname{logit}^{-1}\left(\beta_0 + \sigma\sum_{j=1}^{3} B_j x_{ij}\right),
\qquad Y_i \sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_i).
$$

Here, $\sigma$ is a multiplier applied to the three fixed slopes, not a
standard deviation. The covariates are generated once and reused across all
methods and simulation runs.

# Simulation scenarios

The study crosses two covariate types with two target prevalences. The target
AUC is 0.85 in all four scenarios.

| Scenario | Covariates | Target prevalence | Target AUC |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Binary, low prevalence | Bernoulli(0.5), Bernoulli(0.5), Bernoulli(0.7) | 0.10 | 0.85 |
| Binary, high prevalence | Bernoulli(0.5), Bernoulli(0.5), Bernoulli(0.7) | 0.80 | 0.85 |
| Continuous, low prevalence | Three independent Normal(0, 1) predictors | 0.10 | 0.85 |
| Continuous, high prevalence | Three independent Normal(0, 1) predictors | 0.80 | 0.85 |

Running the chunks evaluates all three algorithms for **all four scenarios**.
Results are retained separately and displayed together for comparison.
Within each covariate type, both prevalence scenarios reuse the same covariate
values through the fixed seed. Algorithm 2 does not use the prevalence target;
its results are therefore the same across the two prevalence scenarios for a
given covariate type, although its deviation from the prevalence target differs.

# Run the code step by step

Open this document in RStudio and run the code chunks in order using the green
arrow on each chunk. Results and plots appear in the interactive session; no
report-generation command is needed. Install `knitr`, `pROC`, `ggplot2`, `dplyr`
and `tidyr` before running the setup chunk. No external data file is required.

Run every chunk in order. The scenario table in the settings chunk defines
all four combinations; no scenario switching or rerunning is required. The
simulation produces 1,200 algorithm runs at the default setting of 100 runs
per method and scenario. For an initial check, set `n.sim <- 2`.

Only one scenario is used for the convergence illustration. The setting
`trace_scenario` defaults to `"binary_prev08"` and can be changed independently
of the four-scenario comparison. No HTML files are generated by these chunks.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 6,
  fig.align = "center"
)

library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

# Simulation settings

The selected target prevalence is either 0.10 or 0.80; the target AUC is 0.85.
The prevalence criterion uses the expected proportion of positive outcomes, `mean(p)`, rather
than the proportion in a single simulated outcome vector. The AUC criterion
uses the average AUC from five simulated outcome vectors per search iteration.

The tolerances specify when a search stops; the iteration limits cap its
runtime. Reaching an iteration limit does not establish that a target was met.

```{r settings}
n.sim <- 100  # simulation runs per algorithm, per scenario
scenarios <- data.frame(
  scenario = c("binary_prev01", "binary_prev08",
               "continuous_prev01", "continuous_prev08"),
  covariate_type = c("binary", "binary", "continuous", "continuous"),
  target_prevalence = c(0.1, 0.8, 0.1, 0.8)
)

# Only this scenario is used for the convergence plots.
trace_scenario <- "binary_prev08"
stopifnot(trace_scenario %in% scenarios$scenario)
if (length(n.sim) != 1L || !is.finite(n.sim) || n.sim < 2 ||
    n.sim != floor(n.sim)) {
  stop("n.sim must be an integer of at least 2 for across-run summaries.")
}

N              <- 5000
target.cstat   <- 0.85
tol.prev       <- 0.0001
tol.cstat      <- 0.0001
max.iter.inner <- 1000
max.iter.outer <- 1000
n.rep.cstat    <- 5       # outcome draws per AUC search iteration
```


# Fixed covariates

For `binary`, the three predictors are independent Bernoulli draws with
probabilities 0.5, 0.5 and 0.7. For `continuous`, all three are independent
standard normal draws. The outcomes remain binary under both covariate types.

`X` includes an intercept column. `B.fixed` supplies the same relative slope
values in every scenario; algorithms 2 and 3 multiply them by a common scalar.
The seed is reset before generating each covariate set, so changing only the
prevalence target does not change `X`.

```{r covariates}
make_covariates <- function(covariate_type, N) {
  set.seed(4555632)
  if (covariate_type == "binary") {
    x1 <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)
    x2 <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)
    x3 <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.7)
  } else {
    x1 <- rnorm(N, mean = 0, sd = 1)
    x2 <- rnorm(N, mean = 0, sd = 1)
    x3 <- rnorm(N, mean = 0, sd = 1)
  }
  cbind(1, x1, x2, x3)
}

# Each prevalence scenario reuses its covariate type's fixed design matrix.
covariates_by_type <- list(
  binary = make_covariates("binary", N),
  continuous = make_covariates("continuous", N)
)

B.fixed <- c(log(2), log(1.2), log(2.8))
```

# Calibration algorithms

## Shared calculations

`det.prev()` calculates expected prevalence for a coefficient vector.
`get.cstat()` calculates AUC from one simulated binary outcome vector and its
probabilities, retaining pROC's default direction selection.

```{r metric-helpers}
det.prev <- function(beta, X) mean(plogis(X %*% beta))

get.cstat <- function(Y, p) {
  # Matrix multiplication produces a one-column matrix; AUC expects a vector.
  as.numeric(pROC::auc(Y, as.numeric(p), quiet = TRUE))
}
```

## Algorithm 1: adjust the intercept

The slope multiplier stays at 1. Bisection searches the intercept interval
[-20, 20], raising or lowering its midpoint according to the expected prevalence.
After the search, one outcome vector is simulated to measure realised prevalence
and AUC. AUC is not targeted by this algorithm.

```{r algorithm-1}
algo1.only <- function(sim.seed) {
  set.seed(sim.seed)
  sigma    <- 1                          # fixed, not optimised
  B.scaled <- sigma * B.fixed
  lo <- -20; hi <- 20

  for (i in seq_len(max.iter.inner)) {
    mid   <- (lo + hi) / 2
    beta  <- c(mid, B.scaled)
    prev  <- det.prev(beta, X)
    if (prev < target.prev) lo <- mid else hi <- mid
    if (abs(prev - target.prev) <= tol.prev) break
  }

  p <- plogis(X %*% c(mid, B.scaled))
  Y <- rbinom(N, 1, p)
  list(prev  = mean(Y),
       cstat = get.cstat(Y, p),
       beta0 = mid,
       sigma = sigma)
}
```

## Algorithm 2: adjust the slope multiplier

The intercept stays at zero. Bisection searches the multiplier interval [0, 20].
At each iteration, AUC is averaged over `n.rep.cstat` simulated outcome vectors.
The final prevalence and AUC are measured using a further outcome draw.
Prevalence is not targeted by this algorithm.

```{r algorithm-2}
algo2.only <- function(sim.seed) {
  set.seed(sim.seed)
  int.fixed <- 0                         # fixed, not optimised
  lo <- 0; hi <- 20

  for (outer in seq_len(max.iter.outer)) {
    sigma    <- (lo + hi) / 2
    B.scaled <- sigma * B.fixed
    beta     <- c(int.fixed, B.scaled)
    p        <- plogis(X %*% beta)

    cstats <- numeric(n.rep.cstat)
    for (r in seq_len(n.rep.cstat)) {
      set.seed(outer * 100 + r + sim.seed)
      Y         <- rbinom(N, 1, p)
      cstats[r] <- get.cstat(Y, p)
    }
    cstat.emp <- mean(cstats)

    if (cstat.emp < target.cstat) lo <- sigma else hi <- sigma
    if (abs(cstat.emp - target.cstat) <= tol.cstat) break
  }

  p <- plogis(X %*% c(int.fixed, B.scaled))
  Y <- rbinom(N, 1, p)
  list(prev  = mean(Y),
       cstat = get.cstat(Y, p),
       beta0 = int.fixed,
       sigma = sigma)
}
```

## Algorithm 3: nested bisection

For every proposed multiplier, an inner search recalibrates the intercept to
the prevalence target. An outer search then updates the multiplier using the
average simulated AUC. Both stopping criteria must be met for an early exit.

The intercept interval remains [-20, 20] and the multiplier interval [0, 20].
The implementation does not expand these intervals or check that the targets
are bracketed. Also, the AUC estimates are stochastic and need not change
monotonically at every iteration. Treat the resulting calibration as an
empirical search and inspect its achieved values.

```{r algorithm-3}
find.intercept <- function(sigma, X, B.fixed, target.prev, tol, max.iter) {
  B.scaled <- sigma * B.fixed
  lo <- -20; hi <- 20
  mid <- 0
  for (i in seq_len(max.iter)) {
    mid  <- (lo + hi) / 2
    prev <- det.prev(c(mid, B.scaled), X)
    if (prev < target.prev) lo <- mid else hi <- mid
    if (abs(prev - target.prev) <= tol) break
  }
  list(intercept = mid, B.scaled = B.scaled, prev = det.prev(c(mid, B.scaled), X))
}

algo3.nested <- function(sim.seed) {
  set.seed(sim.seed)
  lo <- 0; hi <- 20

  for (outer in seq_len(max.iter.outer)) {
    sigma.mid <- (lo + hi) / 2
    inner     <- find.intercept(sigma.mid, X, B.fixed,
                                target.prev, tol.prev, max.iter.inner)
    int.mid   <- inner$intercept
    B.scaled  <- inner$B.scaled
    beta      <- c(int.mid, B.scaled)
    p         <- plogis(X %*% beta)

    cstats <- numeric(n.rep.cstat)
    for (r in seq_len(n.rep.cstat)) {
      set.seed(outer * 100 + r + sim.seed)
      Y         <- rbinom(N, 1, p)
      cstats[r] <- get.cstat(Y, p)
    }
    cstat.emp <- mean(cstats)

    if (cstat.emp < target.cstat) lo <- sigma.mid else hi <- sigma.mid
    if (abs(cstat.emp - target.cstat) <= tol.cstat &&
        abs(inner$prev - target.prev)  <= tol.prev) break
  }

  p <- plogis(X %*% c(int.mid, B.scaled))
  Y <- rbinom(N, 1, p)
  list(prev  = mean(Y),
       cstat = get.cstat(Y, p),
       beta0 = int.mid,
       sigma = sigma.mid)
}
```

# Run the simulations

Each method uses the seed sequence `17, 34, ..., 17 * n.sim`. During AUC
calibration, the seed also depends on the search iteration and the within-iteration
replicate. These choices reproduce the random-number sequence for a fixed R
and package environment; numerical spacing between seeds is not itself an
independence guarantee.

The reported `prev` and `cstat` values come from each method's final outcome
draw. In particular, reported prevalence can differ from the deterministic
prevalence used to calibrate the intercept.

```{r run-simulations}
cat("Running", n.sim, "simulations per method...\n\n")

seeds <- seq_len(n.sim) * 17          # seed for each simulation run

run.sim <- function(algo.fn, label) {
  cat(sprintf("  [%s] ", label))
  out <- lapply(seq_len(n.sim), function(i) {
    if (i %% 100 == 0) cat(i, "")
    algo.fn(seeds[i])
  })
  cat("\n")
  data.frame(
    method = label,
    prev   = sapply(out, `[[`, "prev"),
    cstat  = sapply(out, `[[`, "cstat")
  )}

results_by_scenario <- setNames(vector("list", nrow(scenarios)), scenarios$scenario)

for (scenario_index in seq_len(nrow(scenarios))) {
  current <- scenarios[scenario_index, ]
  # The algorithm functions read the current design matrix and target.
  X <- covariates_by_type[[current$covariate_type]]
  target.prev <- current$target_prevalence
  cat("\nScenario:", current$scenario, "\n")

  res1 <- run.sim(algo1.only, "Algorithm 1 only\n(intercept, fixed σ=1)")
  res2 <- run.sim(algo2.only, "Algorithm 2 only\n(scalar, fixed β₀=0)")
  res3 <- run.sim(algo3.nested, "Algorithm 3\n(nested bisection)")

  scenario_results <- rbind(res1, res2, res3)
  scenario_results$replicate <- rep(seq_len(n.sim), times = 3)
  scenario_results$scenario <- current$scenario
  scenario_results$covariate_type <- current$covariate_type
  scenario_results$target_prevalence <- target.prev
  results_by_scenario[[current$scenario]] <- scenario_results
}

# Keep both the named per-scenario results and a combined data frame.
results <- bind_rows(results_by_scenario)

```

# Summary of target deviations

Bias is the mean realised metric minus its target. SD describes variation
across simulation runs. The table reports each method separately within each scenario.

```{r summary-table}
summary_results <- results %>%
  group_by(scenario, covariate_type, target_prevalence, method) %>%
  summarise(
    prevalence_bias = mean(prev) - first(target_prevalence),
    prevalence_sd = sd(prev),
    auc_bias = mean(cstat) - target.cstat,
    auc_sd = sd(cstat),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(method = gsub("\n", " ", method))

knitr::kable(summary_results, digits = 5, col.names = c(
  "Scenario", "Covariates", "Target prevalence", "Method",
  "Prevalence bias", "Prevalence SD", "AUC bias", "AUC SD"
))
```

# Joint proximity to the targets

Each point represents one simulation run. Diamonds show the method means,
and the cross marks the requested prevalence/AUC pair. The legend reports the
mean Euclidean distance to that pair, giving equal numerical weight to the two
metrics.

The shaded ellipses describe the covariance of the simulated results, using a
95% chi-square contour. They are not confidence regions for the method means
or guarantees of 95% empirical coverage. An ellipse is omitted when either
metric has fewer than three distinct values.

```{r joint-plot-function}
plot_joint <- function(results, target.prev, covariate_type) {
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
cols    <- c("#E63946", "#457B9D", "#2A9D8F")
labels  <- c("Algo. 1 target prevalence",
             "Algo. 2 target AUC",
             "Algo. 3 Both")
methods <- unique(results$method)

pad  <- 0.012
xlim <- range(results$prev)  + c(-pad, pad)
ylim <- range(results$cstat) + c(-pad, pad)
xlim <- c(min(xlim[1], target.prev  - pad), max(xlim[2], target.prev  + pad))
ylim <- c(min(ylim[1], target.cstat - pad), max(ylim[2], target.cstat + pad))

joint.dist <- sapply(seq_along(methods), function(j) {
  d <- results[results$method == methods[j], ]
  mean(sqrt((d$prev - target.prev)^2 + (d$cstat - target.cstat)^2))
})

par(mar = c(5.5, 5.5, 4.5, 2.5), bg = "#FAFAF8", family = "sans")

plot(NULL,
     xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim,
     xlab = "", ylab = "",
     axes = FALSE, asp = NA)

abline(v = target.prev,  col = "#B0B0A0", lwd = 1.2, lty = 2)
abline(h = target.cstat, col = "#B0B0A0", lwd = 1.2, lty = 2)

draw.ellipse <- function(x, y, col, n = 200, level = 0.95) {
  if (length(unique(x)) < 3 || length(unique(y)) < 3) return(invisible())
  S    <- cov(cbind(x, y))
  mu   <- c(mean(x), mean(y))
  ev   <- eigen(S)
  r    <- sqrt(qchisq(level, 2))
  t    <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)
  unit <- cbind(cos(t), sin(t))
  ell  <- t(mu + r * ev$vectors %*% diag(sqrt(ev$values)) %*% t(unit))
  polygon(ell[, 1], ell[, 2],
          col    = adjustcolor(col, 0.08),
          border = adjustcolor(col, 0.45), lwd = 1.2, lty = 1)
}

for (j in seq_along(methods)) {
  d <- results[results$method == methods[j], ]
  draw.ellipse(d$prev, d$cstat, col = cols[j])
  points(d$prev, d$cstat,
         pch = 21,
         bg  = adjustcolor(cols[j], 0.25),
         col = adjustcolor(cols[j], 0.70),
         cex = 0.55, lwd = 0.4)
}

for (j in seq_along(methods)) {
  d <- results[results$method == methods[j], ]
  points(mean(d$prev), mean(d$cstat),
         pch = 23, cex = 2.2,
         bg  = cols[j], col = "white", lwd = 1.5)
}

points(target.prev, target.cstat,
       pch = 3, cex = 1.5, lwd = 2, col = "#1A1A1A")

axis(1, col = "#555555", col.axis = "#333333", cex.axis = 0.85, tcl = -0.3,
     at = pretty(xlim, n = 6))
axis(2, col = "#555555", col.axis = "#333333", cex.axis = 0.85, tcl = -0.3,
     at = pretty(ylim, n = 6), las = 1)
box(col = "#CCCCCC", lwd = 0.8)

mtext("Prevalence", side = 1, line = 3.5, cex = 1.05,
      col = "#333333", font = 2)
mtext("C-statistic (AUC)", side = 2, line = 3.8, cex = 1.05,
      col = "#333333", font = 2)

mtext(sprintf("%s covariates | Target prevalence = %.2f, AUC = %.2f | %d runs per method",
              covariate_type, target.prev, target.cstat, n.sim), font = 2,
      side = 3, line = 1.2, cex = 0.78, col = "#666666")

leg.text <- sprintf("%s  (mean dist = %.4f)", labels, joint.dist)

legend("bottomright",
       legend   = leg.text,
       pch      = 21,
       pt.bg    = adjustcolor(cols, 0.5),
       col      = cols,
       pt.cex   = 1.3,
       cex      = 0.72,
       bty      = "n",
       text.col = "#333333",
       y.intersp = 1.3)

legend("bottomleft",
       legend   = c("Target", "Method mean"),
       pch      = c(3, 23),
       col      = c("#1A1A1A", "#555555"),
       pt.bg    = c(NA, "#888888"),
       pt.cex   = c(1.8, 1.5),
       cex      = 0.72,
       bty      = "n",
       text.col = "#333333")
}
```

Each following chunk displays one scenario. The target and covariate type
are supplied explicitly so each plot uses the correct reference values.

# Trace the nested search

The following trace uses only `trace_scenario`. It repeats algorithm 3 with
seed 17, recording the multiplier,
intercept, scaled slopes, expected prevalence and average AUC at every outer
iteration. This is a calibration trace.The SD of the within-iteration AUC draws 
is recorded for the ribbon below.

```{r calibration-trace}
trace_settings <- scenarios[scenarios$scenario == trace_scenario, ]
X <- covariates_by_type[[trace_settings$covariate_type]]
target.prev <- trace_settings$target_prevalence
cat("Tracking Algorithm 3 for", trace_scenario, "\n")
set.seed(17)
lo <- 0; hi <- 20

conv <- data.frame(
  iter     = integer(), sigma    = double(),
  intercept = double(), coef1   = double(),
  coef2    = double(),  coef3   = double(),
  prev     = double(),  cstat   = double(),
  cstat.sd = double()
)

for (outer in seq_len(max.iter.outer)) {
  sigma.mid <- (lo + hi) / 2
  inner     <- find.intercept(sigma.mid, X, B.fixed,
                              target.prev, tol.prev, max.iter.inner)
  int.mid   <- inner$intercept
  B.scaled  <- inner$B.scaled
  p         <- plogis(X %*% c(int.mid, B.scaled))

  cstats <- numeric(n.rep.cstat)
  for (r in seq_len(n.rep.cstat)) {
    set.seed(outer * 100 + r + 17)
    Y         <- rbinom(N, 1, p)
    cstats[r] <- get.cstat(Y, p)
  }
  cstat.emp <- mean(cstats)
  if (cstat.emp < target.cstat) lo <- sigma.mid else hi <- sigma.mid

  conv <- rbind(conv, data.frame(
    iter = outer, sigma = sigma.mid, intercept = int.mid,
    coef1 = B.scaled[1], coef2 = B.scaled[2], coef3 = B.scaled[3],
    prev = inner$prev, cstat = cstat.emp, cstat.sd = sd(cstats)
  ))

  if (abs(cstat.emp  - target.cstat) <= tol.cstat &&
      abs(inner$prev - target.prev)  <= tol.prev) {
    cat(sprintf("Converged after %d iterations.\n", outer)); break
  }
}
```

```{r trace-status}
last_step <- conv[nrow(conv), ]
met_targets <- abs(last_step$prev - target.prev) <= tol.prev &&
  abs(last_step$cstat - target.cstat) <= tol.cstat

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  iterations = nrow(conv),
  expected_prevalence = last_step$prev,
  average_auc = last_step$cstat,
  both_tolerances_met = met_targets
), digits = 5)
```

## Plot styling

A common theme is used for the four trace plots.

```{r plot-theme}
base_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey30", color = "black"),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "#FAFAF8", colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FAFAF8", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#E8E8E4", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = "#F0F0EC", linewidth = 0.2),
    axis.title       = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#333333", size = 9.5),
    axis.text        = element_text(colour = "#555555", size = 8.5),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1A1A1A", size = 11,
                                    hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 2)),
    legend.position  = "none",
    plot.margin      = margin(4, 12, 4, 8)
  )
```

## Expected prevalence

The dashed line marks the target. These are the deterministic prevalence values
from the inner intercept searches, rather than realised outcome proportions.

```{r trace-prevalence}
p_prev <- ggplot(conv, aes(x = iter, y = prev)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target.prev,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#333333", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "#0077BB", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(colour = "#0077BB", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Iteration") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Prevalence") +
  labs(title = "Prevalence") +
  base_theme

p_prev
```

## Average AUC

The dashed line marks the AUC target. The ribbon spans the average AUC plus or
minus one SD across the outcome draws at each iteration. It is not a confidence
interval or a standard-error band.

```{r trace-auc}
p_auc <- ggplot(conv, aes(x = iter, y = cstat)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target.cstat,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#333333", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = cstat - cstat.sd,
                  ymax = cstat + cstat.sd),
              fill = "#E63946", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(colour = "#E63946", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(colour = "#E63946", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Iteration") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "C-statistic (AUC)") +
  labs(title = "AUC") +
  base_theme

p_auc
```

## Intercept

The dashed line marks the final recorded intercept, providing a reference for
the search path. It does not establish that calibration succeeded.

```{r trace-intercept}
p_int <- ggplot(conv, aes(x = iter, y = intercept)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tail(conv$intercept, 1),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#555555", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(colour = "#111111", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(colour = "#111111", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Iteration") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = expression(beta[0])) +
  labs(title = "Intercept") +
  base_theme

p_int
```

## Scaled slopes

The three curves show the fixed slopes multiplied by the proposed scalar.
Their relative sizes remain constant throughout calibration.

```{r trace-slopes}
param_cols <- c(
  "coef1" = "#E63946",
  "coef2" = "#F4A500",
  "coef3" = "#0077BB"
)

slopes_df <- conv %>%
  select(iter, coef1, coef2, coef3) %>%
  pivot_longer(-iter, names_to = "slope", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(slope = factor(slope, levels = names(param_cols)))

p_slopes <- ggplot(slopes_df, aes(x = iter, y = value, colour = slope)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = param_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Iteration") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Scaled slope") +
  labs(title = "Slopes") +
  base_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(colour = "Slope")

p_slopes
```
